name: argument-parser-positive-test-e41e5b8a0a/int-positive-v
spec_references: Module-level declarations: "Supports [`required-params`](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#required-params), [`defaultable-params`](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#defaultable-params), [`included-record-param`](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#included-record-param) and [`rest-param`](https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/#rest-param) in the signature"

Invocations / Named and default arguments: "Named arguments and omitted defaultable arguments are supported for function calls when the callee has an atomic function type with a known parameter signature."
reason: The test requires the executable entry-point protocol to parse command-line string "10" as int, pass it to main(int i), and print 10. Subset 10 supports required parameter signatures and ordinary invocations but does not cover command-line argument parsing or binding to main; signature support does not establish that execution behavior.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line argument conversion and binding to typed main parameters (@args ["10"] -> main(int i)).
test_design_notes: @output 10 asserts successful entry-point argument parsing; io:println is instrumentation and is not the feature gap.
